cards.text: Just before this, the people of Bethel asked whether they should keep weeping and fasting in the fifth month (Zechariah 7:3). The word of the LORD came to Zechariah, a prophet, asking if those fasts were really for God, and reminding them how people refused to listen to the earlier prophets (Zechariah 7:5, 11-12). Now the word of the LORD of Hosts comes to Zechariah AGAIN, and friend, I'm leaning in like it's the last ten seconds on the oven timer.
First thing God says: "I am jealous for Zion with great zeal; I am jealous for her with great fervor." Zion is Jerusalem, friend, and after all that refusing to listen, THIS is how He opens.

cards.question: God says He is jealous for Zion with great zeal. True or false: that means He has given up on her.
God has big feelings about Zion. What does He say He will do there?

answers.text: Scatter His people from it again
Hand it over to a new king

cards.text: Then, God says, Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth. Big upgrade, friend, because the best name I got in the junk drawer I was stuck in for years was 'that thing under the takeout menus.'

cards.question: With the LORD dwelling in Jerusalem, what will the mountain of the LORD of Hosts be called?
God paints a picture of Jerusalem's future. What will old men and old women, each with a staff in hand, do again?
Old folks will sit along the streets. And God says the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls ___ there.

cards.text: Then God asks a question. If this is impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be impossible in His eyes?

cards.question: God asks if what looks impossible to the remnant should be impossible to Him too. What's His point?

answers.text: The promise may not come true

cards.text: Next God says, "I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west." His people are scattered east AND west, friend, like my sprinkles the time I opened the jar upside down.

cards.question: God says He will bring His people back to dwell in Jerusalem, where they will be His people, and He will be their faithful and righteous God. True or false?

cards.text: Now God speaks to everyone hearing these words from the prophets who were there when the foundations were laid to rebuild the temple, the house of the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: What does God tell the people hearing the prophets who were there at the temple's foundations?

answers.text: Let the work rest a while

cards.text: Then God looks back to before those days, when neither man nor beast received wages, and no one who came or went was safe from the enemy. Friend, when even the BEASTS aren't getting a paycheck, that's a rough economy.

cards.question: True or false: God says that back then, He had turned every man against his neighbor.

cards.text: But now God says He will not treat the remnant of this people as He did in the past. My favorite kind of sentence, friend, is the one that starts with 'but now.'

cards.question: God won't treat the remnant the way He did in the past. So what does He promise them?

answers.text: Their enemies will bring them gold

cards.text: The seed will be prosperous, the vine will yield its fruit, the ground its produce, and the skies their dew. And God says He will give all of it to the remnant as an inheritance.

cards.question: The house of Judah and the house of Israel have been a curse among the nations. Now God says He will save them, and they will be a ___.

cards.text: Then God says, "Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong." There's 'let your hands be strong' again, and friend, my hands are a MUSTACHE, so I am doing curls RIGHT NOW.
Then God looks back again. When their fathers provoked Him to anger, He resolved to bring disaster on the very people He's now talking to.

cards.question: True or false: when the fathers provoked God to anger, He resolved to bring disaster on His people, and then He relented.
God resolved on disaster back then and didn't back down. So what has He resolved to do now?

answers.text: Do good again to Jerusalem and Judah
Wait and see how Judah behaves
Bring disaster on all the nations

cards.text: And again: "Do not be afraid." Friend, after years in a junk drawer flinching every time it opened, I could hear that one ALL day.

cards.question: God says, "These are the things you must do…" What's the first thing on His list?

answers.text: Build a wall around the city
Offer more sacrifices at the temple

cards.text: They're also to render true and sound judgments in their gates, not plot evil in their hearts against their neighbor, and not love to swear falsely. Read that last one again, friend: not just don't swear falsely, but don't LOVE to.

cards.question: God tells them not to plot evil against their neighbor or love to swear falsely, for He ___ all these things.

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts comes to Zechariah again. Friend, I haven't left the edge of my seat since the first time.

cards.question: God names the fasts of the fourth, the fifth, the seventh and the tenth months. What does He say those fasts will become?

cards.text: God says those fasts will become cheerful feasts for the house of Judah. Friend, that's like opening your calendar and finding the gloomiest dates turned into PARTIES.

cards.question: Judah's fasts will become cheerful feasts. Because of that, what does God tell them to love?

cards.text: Then God looks ahead. Peoples will yet come, the residents of many cities.

cards.question: The residents of one city will go to another city. What will they say?

answers.text: Let us go and seek the LORD
Let us go and trade in Jerusalem
Let us go and see the new walls

cards.question: The residents of one city invite another to go at once to plead before the LORD. True or false: the ones doing the inviting plan to go too.

cards.text: The ones doing the inviting say, "I myself am going." That's the friend who's already in your driveway with the engine running, honking at YOU.

cards.question: True or false: God says only a few small nations will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem.

cards.text: Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to plead before the LORD. We started with one friend in the driveway, and now it's a whole HIGHWAY of nations.

One last picture: in those days, ten men from the nations of every tongue will tightly grasp the robe of a Jew. Ten grown men on ONE robe, friend, that's the same grip I've got on the last cookie in the box.

cards.question: These men from the nations will hold on tightly to the robe of a Jew. What reason will they give?

answers.text: We have heard that God is with you
We have lost our way in the city
We have come to collect a debt
